guarantees.claim: The error code register is updated with err_code and its data enable is driven by err_valid.

The hash_start and hash_continue outputs are asserted only when reg_hash_start/reg_hash_continue is high, sha_en is high, cfg_block is low, and invalid_config is low. hash_process is asserted only when reg_hash_process is high, sha_en is high, cfg_block is high, and invalid_config is low. hash_start_or_continue is the OR of hash_start and hash_continue.

formal.consequent: hash_start == (reg_hash_start & sha_en & !cfg_block & !invalid_config) && hash_continue == (reg_hash_continue & sha_en & !cfg_block & !invalid_config) && hash_process == (reg_hash_process & sha_en & cfg_block & !invalid_config) && hash_start_or_continue == (hash_start | hash_continue)

formal_sketch.consequent: hash_start == (reg_hash_start & sha_en & !cfg_block & !invalid_config) && hash_continue == (reg_hash_continue & sha_en & !cfg_block & !invalid_config) && hash_process == (reg_hash_process & sha_en & cfg_block & !invalid_config) && hash_start_or_continue == (hash_start | hash_continue)

assumptions.claim: The reg2hw.cmd write qualifier signals (qe) are single-cycle pulses that go high only when the corresponding command register is written.
assumptions.cond: when a hash command is issued
assumptions.risk: If qe remains high for multiple cycles, the command strobe signals (reg_hash_start, etc.) could be asserted continuously, causing repeated hash operations or state machine corruption.

assumptions.claim: The sha_en, cfg_block, and invalid_config signals correctly reflect the engine's operational state and configuration validity at all times.
assumptions.cond: before and during hash command assertion
assumptions.risk: If invalid_config is incorrectly deasserted while the configuration is actually invalid, the HMAC engine could start or continue processing with a bad configuration, leading to wrong MAC generation or potential key/digest leakage.

formal_sketch.antecedent: before and during hash command assertion
formal_sketch.consequent: The sha_en, cfg_block, and invalid_config signals correctly reflect the engine's operational state and configuration validity at all times

assumptions.claim: The digest_size and key_length signals shall always be within the valid enumeration ranges of digest_mode_e and key_length_e, respectively.
assumptions.cond: whenever the hw2reg.cfg readback is driven
assumptions.risk: Casting an out-of-range value to the enum type may produce an undefined or illegal enum label, causing downstream logic that consumes these status fields to misbehave, with unknown security consequences.

formal_sketch.antecedent: whenever the hw2reg.cfg readback is driven

uncertain_points.claim: The hash command gating logic does not take err_valid or any error state into account; if a hardware error is latched but invalid_config is not asserted, the engine may still start or continue hash operations.
uncertain_points.risk: An HMAC operation could proceed with corrupted or faulted internal state, leading to incorrect MAC output or exposure of cryptographic material.

uncertain_points.claim: The hw2reg.cfg.digest_size.d and hw2reg.cfg.key_length.d assignments use type casts to digest_mode_e and key_length_e without checking that the input signals are within the legal enum ranges.
uncertain_points.cond: digest_size or key_length not matching a legal enum member
uncertain_points.risk: The readback fields could take undefined or unexpected values, confusing software or downstream FSM logic that relies on these enums being valid.

security_implications: The hash command gating (hash_start/continue/process) relies on sha_en, cfg_block, and invalid_config to prevent HMAC operations during unsafe conditions. If invalid_config is not asserted when configuration is invalid, the engine could operate with a bad config, potentially revealing secret keys through incorrect MAC tags or producing integrity-damaged digests. Additionally, the absence of error-state gating means a latent hardware fault (err_valid) may not stop further hash processing, increasing the risk of using corrupted cryptographic state. The hw2reg.cfg readback includes security-sensitive fields (key_swap, digest_swap) that could be misreported if upstream signals are invalid, misleading software. This chunk is directly in the HMAC control path and must satisfy high integrity requirements.
